Original project-authored fictional Turn Structure V2. Not real Magic rules authority.
Supported windows in order: beginning/untap, beginning/upkeep, beginning/draw, main/action, ending/end. No combat or other omitted Magic steps, first-player draw exception, triggered upkeep abilities, replacements or complete Magic turn compliance.
End-to-next-turn advancement changes active player and enters untap with no priority and exactly untap_active_player queued. The existing native untap primitive untaps eligible known unrestricted battlefield objects controlled by the active player, then changes to upkeep with progress upkeep and active-player priority. Inactive controlled objects do not untap.
Upkeep uses existing priority and stack behavior. Only two passes with an empty stack may queue advancement after the checkpoint. A supported instant may be cast/paid/resolved through existing primitives; stack resolution leaves upkeep unchanged and returns priority. Another pass cycle is required to leave upkeep.
Advancement from upkeep enters draw with no priority and queues draw_for_turn then perform_state_based_actions. Exactly the first explicitly ordered library object moves into its owner's hand and controller becomes that player. Empty library remains unsupported, without a loss rule. The checkpoint finishes before active-player priority. A further pass cycle is required to enter main/action. Existing land/sorcery timing is unchanged.
Progress binds turn number and active player. pending_untap, upkeep, pending_draw and complete states have exact window/queue constraints. Complete cannot repeat untap or draw. Settled initial positions are explicit inputs, not authenticated historical events. No shuffling, text execution or strategic inference.
The separate fictional blue-pebble demonstration semantics reuse the existing add_mana primitive with an explicit one-blue amount and tap cost. This supplies the existing swift-lantern instant's written one-blue cost; it adds no new engine effect.
